newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Australian prices flat in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Australian prices flat in quiet market.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board's (AWB) national indicator price declined to A$191.00 a tonne fob from a high of A$196.00 in the latest week, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in its weekly report.
Australian domestic markets were quiet with an absence of grower selling of new and old crop wheat, it said.

Old crop markets in South Australia, Victoria and southern New South Wales were slightly stronger but dry conditions and a lack of a break in the weather continued to drive a reluctance in the market, it said.
Farmers in Australia's eastern states were re-applying for drought assistance as a result of the current dry weather, it said.
The market was up a little across all commodities, ranging between A$1.00 and A$3.00 a tonne.
Milling was quiet and little interest was shown in multigrade wheat.
The AWB offered to buy back a guaranteed five percent of individual grower's equity in the Wheat Industry Fund for the fourth consecutive year, it said.

Chicago's wheat futures market rally on Wednesday was the result of lower wheat planting forecasts in Australia, Argentina and Canada and to the developing El Nino dry weather pattern in Australia, it said.

"The market's volatility has been attributed to the dry weather conditions in Europe and to some extent Australia and Argentina and uncertainty regarding damage to the Hard Red Winter (HRW) wheat crop," it said.
The Kansas market for HRW wheat last week saw record trading volume for April, attributed to volatility associated with recent crop damage in the HRW areas, it said.
